Reference Petition Under Section 18 Of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
J U D G M E N T / Awar D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the
Act"), filed by the petitioners men
tioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose
. The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 14 of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The said land is surrounded by the well developed the areas having all basic modern facilities i.e. well connected roads, adequate transport facility, hospitals, schools, colleges, reputed clubs, farmhouses, party lawns and banquet Halls and is, therefore, having the market value @ Rs. 8000 per square yards and the agricultural land was sold at this rate in the surrounding areas.

The NH 10 is 2 kms away from the said land, the bottling plant of Indian Gas and FCI godown is around 3 kms from the said land, and Mundka, Udyog Vihar,
metro workstation is around 2 kms from the said land, Railway Station Mundka and other developed areas having all the transport facilities and basic amenities are around 1 kms from the said land.

These factors leads to inescapable conclusion that the said land be valued @ Rs. 8000/

sentences.text: The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
It is stated that DDA is not liable to pay compensation as the said land has not been taken over by the DDA either due to stay by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
17. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been handed over to DDA on 15.12.2005 and after taking the possession, the same has been transferred to RPDVII.

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
23.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioners, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ram Kishan (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
24. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
25. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

entities.text: Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

26. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
27. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
RELIEF LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 28.

LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 8.
It is also submitted that ld. LAC failed to appreciate that it is the distance and the potentiality of the land and not the village, which is to be kept in mind LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 while awarding the compensation.
11. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money and the ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioners.
The ld. LAC has grossly erred in deducting the tax, as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.
LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 14 12.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ? OPP 2. Relief.
19.
My issuewise findings and determination are as under:  LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 238 of 2016 Ram Kishan v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.
Counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
23.
25. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
27. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
RELIEF LAC no. 61 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satyavir & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 28.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
